title: When the Regiment Burns
premise: Beatrix Vane, a suffragist's driver in 1913 London, reads every letter she carries, and one day a stranger named Elias Thorn arrives with a letter in the unmistakable hand of Captain Rowan Vane — her brother, officially dead at Ypres two years before. The letter implicates a regimental quartermaster in selling supplies and falsifying casualty lists, and Rowan is alive, hiding, and hunted. Elias, a demobilized soldier with nothing left to lose, must smuggle the letter and its corroborating ledger past three checkpoints to reach Parliament before a vote buries the inquiry forever. Betrayed at the second checkpoint, Beatrix and Elias finish the run together; Rowan testifies, the quartermaster falls, and Beatrix — who inherited her brother's silence — finally claims a family of her own making.
about_author: Paloma Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing soldiers' unsent letters in regional collections. She writes from a converted stable in Yorkshire, where she keeps her grandmother's suffrage sash framed above the desk.

chapters.title: The Driver's Privilege
chapters.summary: Beatrix Vane, POV. Introduces her double life: chauffeur for suffragist Honoria Ashe by day, secret reader of every letter by habit. She steams open an envelope out of routine and finds nothing remarkable — establishing her skill, her loneliness, and her rule never to interfere. Beat: competence masking grief.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Mews
chapters.summary: Elias Thorn, POV. A gaunt ex-soldier arrives at the Ashe house mews asking for 'the driver who reads.' He carries a sealed letter he was told only she could authenticate. Beatrix recognizes the handwriting instantly: her brother Rowan's, dead two years. Beat: the ground tilts.

chapters.title: Dead Men's Ink
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She compares the letter against old family letters hidden in her trunk — same slanted f's, same ink habit. Elias explains he received it from a dying hospital orderly in Calais. Emotional beat: hope arriving as a wound, because hope is dangerous.

chapters.title: What the Letter Says
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The letter names Quartermaster Aldous Grebe: falsified casualty rolls, sold regimental stores, men left unrecorded so their pay could be pocketed. Rowan is alive, hiding under another name. Beat: Beatrix must choose between safety and her brother.

chapters.title: Miss Ashe's War
chapters.summary: Honoria Ashe, POV. Honoria is preparing testimony for a parliamentary inquiry into army administration. She doesn't know about the letter yet. We see the political machinery, the timelines, the vote that will kill the inquiry in six weeks. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias negotiates: he'll carry the letter and a stolen quartermaster's ledger to a contact at the War Office, but he wants Beatrix's protection — Grebe's men are already asking after him in the pubs. Beat: reluctant alliance, two people testing each other's nerve.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She and Elias decode the ledger: numbers that match dead men's names, including men from her village. The abstract crime becomes personal. Beat: grief converted to fury; the found-family theme begins to bind them.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: Dover Road
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The journey begins. At a military police stop on the Dover road, Elias talks his way through using forged discharge papers Beatrix prepared. Tension established; his hands shake after. Beat: fear acknowledged, courage chosen anyway.

chapters.title: The Man Who Follows
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Back in London, Beatrix notices a watcher outside the mews — Sergeant Crake, Grebe's fixer. She leads him on a chase through the tram lines. Beat: Beatrix stops being a bystander in her own story.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. On a night train, Elias confesses why he took this job: his own brother is one of the unrecorded dead in the ledger. Beatrix, reading this in a letter he leaves behind, understands him fully. Beat: two griefs recognize each other.

chapters.title: Honoria's Bargain
chapters.summary: Honoria, POV. Honoria discovers Beatrix's secret reading habit and, instead of dismissing her, offers the movement's protection — if the evidence reaches her in time to use. Beat: Beatrix is seen, valued, and recruited; the family widens.

chapters.title: The Safe House in Canterbury
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias shelters with a Quaker innkeeper who owes Rowan a debt. He learns Rowan has been moving, hunted, leaving a trail of small kindnesses. Beat: the absent brother becomes vivid through others' memories — inheritance of reputation.

chapters.title: Crake Closes In
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Crake confronts Beatrix at a suffrage meeting, offering her brother's safety in exchange for the ledger's location. She lies fluently and hates how good she's become at it. Beat: the enemy humanized slightly; stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Ashford Yard
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. At Ashford rail yard, a sympathetic porter warns that Grebe's men hold the southbound platform. Elias hides the ledger in a coffin bound for a military funeral. Beat: macabre irony; the dead literally carry the truth of the dead.

chapters.title: The Coffin Route
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix travels to Ashford posing as the widow's sister to retrieve the ledger from the funeral procession. A near-discovery in the vestry. Beat: audacity as grief-work; she touches the coffin and thinks of Rowan.

chapters.title: What Rowan Carried
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. A flashback chapter: how Rowan survived, how he gathered the ledger, how he passed it to the dying orderly with one instruction — find the reader. Beat: the brother's sacrifice reframes Beatrix's inheritance of silence.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Third Milestone
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The innkeeper's nephew sells their route to Crake. Elias is ambushed; the ledger is nearly taken; he escapes wounded, losing the forged papers. Beat: trust broken; the cost of the mission becomes blood.

chapters.title: The Wound and the Wait
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix finds Elias feverish in a Lambeth lodging house and nurses him. He deliriously calls her by his dead brother's name. Beat: tenderness under pressure; the found family solidifies around a sickbed.

chapters.title: Grebe's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: Honoria, POV. Honoria attends a dinner where Grebe is guest of honor and plays the devoted servant of the regiment. She watches him work the room and understands the vote is already bought. Beat: elegant menace; the enemy's power made visible.

chapters.title: A Name in the Roll
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix visits the War Office records room under pretense of family paperwork and finds her brother's death certificate — signed by Grebe. Beat: cold fury; the personal crime documented in official ink.

chapters.title: The Vote Is Set
chapters.summary: Honoria, POV. The inquiry vote is scheduled in nine days. Honoria lays out the plan: evidence must be tabled before the session opens, no exceptions. Beat: the ticking clock made explicit; allies commit.

chapters.title: Repairing the Route
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias and Beatrix plan a new route avoiding all known checkpoints — a barge down the Medway, then overland. He insists on going alone; she refuses. Beat: argument that is really about fear of losing each other.

chapters.title: Crake's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Crake, more desperate, reveals Grebe knows Rowan is alive and has men hunting him in France. The choice: deliver the ledger and expose Rowan's location, or protect Rowan and lose the inquiry. Beat: the trap's teeth show.

chapters.title: The Barge at Snodland
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The barge journey: quiet water, shared watch, Elias teaching Beatrix to read river signals. A patrol boat passes in the night. Beat: stillness before the storm; intimacy without declaration.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: Chatham Gate
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The final checkpoint at Chatham docks. Beatrix distracts the sergeant with a fabricated suffrage delegation while Elias walks the ledger through inside a mail sack. Beat: her skills and his nerve finally working as one.

chapters.title: The Contact Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The War Office contact is dead — 'accident,' three days prior. The ledger has nowhere to go. Elias realizes only Parliament itself, and Honoria, remain. Beat: the plan collapses; despair's floor.

chapters.title: Reading the Room
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix proposes the unthinkable: give the ledger to the newspapers Honoria despises, forcing Parliament's hand. Honoria must choose between respectability and victory. Beat: the mentor's crisis; strategy born from the driver's low view of institutions.

chapters.title: Honoria Decides
chapters.summary: Honoria, POV. Honoria burns her careful speech and drafts a new one around the ledger's numbers. She formally takes Beatrix and Elias into her confidence — not staff, but comrades. Beat: hierarchy dissolves into family; the theme lands.

chapters.title: Crake at the Door
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Crake raids the Ashe house with a warrant. The ledger is hidden in plain sight, rebound as a suffrage membership book. Beatrix watches him hold it and put it down. Beat: unbearable suspense; her steadiest hour.

chapters.title: Rowan's Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. The night before the vote, Beatrix finally reads Rowan's letter aloud to the assembled household. It ends with a message for her: 'You were always the brave one; you just did it quietly.' Beat: catharsis; inheritance redefined as courage passed down.

chapters.title: The Morning of the Vote
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Westminster in fog. Grebe's men thicken the lobby. Honoria's carriage is delayed — deliberately. Beatrix takes the wheel herself. Beat: the driver drives; every skill she's hidden becomes the mission's spine.

chapters.title: Through the Lobby
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias carries the ledger on foot through the crowd while Beatrix draws Crake's men with a decoy route in the motor. A foot chase across Westminster Bridge. Beat: split-screen tension; both risk everything.

chapters.title: Climax: The Tabled Evidence
chapters.summary: Honoria, POV. Honoria rises in the committee room as the vote is called, and tables the ledger. Grebe demands its seizure; the numbers speak for themselves; members waver, then turn. Beat: climax — truth, delivered at the last possible minute, breaks the machine.

chapters.title: Grebe's Fall
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Grebe is arrested on the steps; Crake, offered testimony, trades Grebe for himself and confirms Rowan's location. Beat: justice without triumphalism; even victory tastes like ash.

chapters.title: The Man from the Train
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. A thin, scarred man waits at Victoria Station. Beatrix walks past him twice before she recognizes her brother. No embrace at first — just his hand on her shoulder, the old gesture. Beat: reunion rendered small and enormous.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Undone
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Rowan explains his years of hiding; the dead in the ledger stay dead; the inquiry will take years. Beatrix grieves the time that can't be returned. Beat: the cost honored; no cheap healing.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rowan Vane, POV. Rowan testifies before the inquiry, naming names. Beatrix and Elias watch from the gallery. Honoria's movement gains a public victory it will spend for a decade. Beat: public reckoning; private relief.

chapters.title: The Mews in Spring
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Months later: Honoria offers Beatrix a partnership running the movement's courier network. Elias stays on as mechanic. The household re-forms around a shared table. Beat: the found family becomes ordinary, which is its triumph.

chapters.title: Letters Worth Reading
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix opens the post one morning and finds a letter from Rowan, alive and nearby — the first letter she'll read without fear. She reads it twice, then files it with the others she's kept. Beat: memory kept deliberately; inheritance chosen.

chapters.title: When the Regiment Burns
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, final chapter. At a memorial for the ledger's unrecorded men, their names are read aloud for the first time. Beatrix adds her brother's service record to the archive, corrected in her own hand. She drives home with the windows down. Beat: resolution — memory as inheritance, family as the thing you build and keep.
